notes: 29 of the 31 assertions pass with and without the skill, so they show a floor both reach, not the difference. The model without the skill already drops capitals, defines done by the check and keeps the boundaries.

The two assertions that differ: without the skill, the goal tells the agent what to read first and how to debug a pixel difference, and the trimmed AGENTS.md keeps the directory layout and dependency list.

The larger differences are ones a person has to judge. Release-notes skill: without the skill it is a seven-step procedure of 1,348 words; with the skill it opens with the two facts people get wrong and is 891 words. AGENTS.md: 553 words without, 330 with. Goal: 615 words without, 798 with (the skill adds the split between ordinary and protected obstacles, a notes file, and a list of what needs no approval).
Cost: runs with the skill used about 28% more tokens (84,000 against 65,600 on average) and took about 49% longer (125 seconds against 84).
One run per configuration. This is a smoke test; differences this small need two or three runs each to trust.
Two runs with the skill listed the skill folder and saw the grader file names under evals/. Neither opened a grader. Next round, tell runs not to list evals/.

Gaps the runs reported in the skill: 'write whole sentences' pulls against 'keep the instruction file short'; the 2-space indentation line is given as a good example and also fits 'a line the reader would have followed anyway'; no guidance on git actions (branch, push) in a goal; no guidance for a rule whose real condition the writer doesn't know.
